title: Cerebellar examination
stem: Cubicle 24. Mr Man, 66, with hypertension and diabetes, developed sudden unsteadiness, vomiting and slurred speech 3 hours ago. Perform a cerebellar examination and explain your findings.

phases.title: Present and plan
phases.goal: Where is the lesion, what is it, and what now?

notes:
Checked against standard neurological examination and ESO/AHA stroke guidance on posterior circulation stroke.

Cerebellar signs (DANISH): Dysdiadochokinesia, Ataxia (gait, truncal), Nystagmus, Intention tremor and past-pointing, Slurred (scanning) speech, Hypotonia (and pendular reflexes). Also heel–shin, tandem gait, Romberg (positive in sensory or vestibular ataxia, not typically in pure cerebellar disease — a cerebellar patient is unsteady with eyes open too). Signs are ipsilateral to a cerebellar hemisphere lesion; midline (vermis) lesions give truncal ataxia.

Sudden cerebellar signs with vascular risk factors: cerebellar infarct or haemorrhage — emergency CT and CT angiography (MRI DWI is more sensitive for posterior strokes), stroke team (thrombolysis/thrombectomy for basilar occlusion), and neurosurgery for cerebellar haemorrhage over 3 cm or hydrocephalus — the posterior fossa is small and swelling compresses the brainstem.

Your notes list the full cerebellar examination and causes (unilateral: vascular, tumour, MS; bilateral: alcohol, phenytoin, Wernicke's, MS, Miller Fisher, paraneoplastic) — this matches.

Perfect script checked against the DANISH cerebellar examination and stroke pathway, an HKCEM-style scheme and a keyword scheme. Gait is not tested: he cannot sit unsupported, so walking him is unsafe; the plan says when it would be.

A focused 3D examination: each manoeuvre is shown being done, the right-sided signs on the patient (intention tremor and past-pointing, dysdiadochokinesia, a floppy right arm, the heel slipping off the shin, nystagmus beating to the right, leaning to the right when sat up).

body.intro: Mr Man lies in bed, pale, a vomit bowl beside him. Examine his cerebellar system: choose below.

findings.finger-nose@pulp-R: Right: the finger shakes more the nearer it gets to yours, and overshoots: intention tremor and past-pointing.
findings.tone-arm@forearm-R: Right arm: floppy; the hand flops about at the wrist.
findings.heel-shin@heel-R: Right heel: wobbles from side to side and slips off the shin.
findings.heel-shin@heel-L: Left heel: runs smoothly down the shin.
findings.tone-leg@thigh-R: Right leg: floppy as it rolls.
findings.grip: Grip strong and equal on both sides.

steps.label: Examine
steps.hint: Speech and eyes; arms (finger–nose, rapid alternating, tone); legs (heel–shin, tone); sitting balance; then power and sensation.

Speech and eyes.r: "Bri… tish… con… sti… tu… tion": slurred and broken into syllables, staccato: a cerebellar dysarthria.

Speech and eyes.t: Eye movements: keep your head still and follow my finger.
Speech and eyes.r: Horizontal nystagmus, the fast phase to the right, worst looking right; a beat or two looking left. No double vision.

Arms.t: Finger–nose test: touch my finger, then your nose, as quickly and accurately as you can. Now the other hand.
Arms.r: Right: the finger shakes more as it nears mine, and overshoots past it: intention tremor and past-pointing. Left: smooth and accurate.
Arms.mark: Finger–nose test, both sides: right intention tremor

Arms.t: Rapid alternating movements: pat your thighs, front then back, as fast as you can.
Arms.r: Left quick and even; right slow, irregular and clumsy, not turning fully over: dysdiadochokinesia on the right.

Arms.t: Tone: let me bend and straighten your elbow, and roll your leg.
Arms.r: Reduced on the right: the right hand flops about at the wrist and the leg rolls floppily. Left normal.

Legs.t: Heel–shin test: put your heel on the other knee, and run it down your shin. Now the other side.
Legs.r: Right heel wobbles from side to side and slips off the shin; left smooth.

Trunk.t: Truncal ataxia: sit up and fold your arms, without holding on. I'm right here.
Trunk.r: He sways and leans over to the right, and needs my hand to stop him falling: truncal ataxia.

To complete.t: Power and sensation: squeeze my fingers; and can you feel this sharp?
To complete.r: Grip strong and equal; sharp touch felt normally: no weakness or sensory loss.

steps.ask: Thank you. Please present your findings and your plan.
steps.label: Present and plan
steps.hint: Right cerebellar syndrome, sudden onset: stroke pathway, CT/CTA, neurosurgery if haemorrhage; gait only when safe.

opts.t: Right-sided cerebellar signs of sudden onset in a vascular patient: dysarthria, nystagmus, intention tremor, dysdiadochokinesia, hypotonia, heel–shin ataxia and truncal ataxia. A right cerebellar stroke until proven otherwise.
opts.mark: Localises to the right cerebellum and suspects stroke

opts.t: Stroke team now; urgent CT head and CT angiogram of the basilar and vertebral arteries.
If it's a haemorrhage over 3 cm or there's hydrocephalus: neurosurgery. Close GCS monitoring.
I haven't walked him: he can't sit without support, so it isn't safe. Gait, heel–toe walking and Romberg once he can.
opts.mark: Tests gait only when it is safe

badge.name: DANISH
badge.flavor: Same-side signs. Sudden onset in a vascular patient: scan the back of the brain.

cards.q: Imaging most sensitive for posterior circulation infarct?
cards.why: CT misses many early posterior strokes.

cards.q: Cerebellar haemorrhage > 3 cm with deterioration needs…

options: At the end of a movement

script.say: Speech: say 'British constitution' for me. Eye movements: keep your head still and follow my finger.
script.do: Slurred, staccato speech. Horizontal nystagmus, fast phase to the right, worst looking right.

script.say: Finger–nose test: touch my finger, then your nose, as quickly and accurately as you can. Now the other hand. Rapid alternating movements: pat your thighs, front then back, as fast as you can. Tone: let me bend and straighten your elbow, and roll your leg.
script.do: Right: intention tremor and past-pointing; dysdiadochokinesia; reduced tone. Left normal.

script.say: Heel–shin test: put your heel on the other knee, and run it down your shin. Now the other side. Truncal ataxia: sit up and fold your arms, without holding on. I'm right here. Power and sensation: squeeze my fingers; and can you feel this sharp?
script.do: Right heel wobbles off the shin. Leans to the right sitting, needs support. Power and sensation normal.

script.say: Right-sided cerebellar signs of sudden onset in a vascular patient: dysarthria, nystagmus, intention tremor, dysdiadochokinesia, hypotonia, heel–shin ataxia and truncal ataxia. A right cerebellar stroke until proven otherwise. Stroke team now; urgent CT head and CT angiogram of the basilar and vertebral arteries. If it's a haemorrhage over 3 cm or there's hydrocephalus: neurosurgery. Close GCS monitoring. I haven't walked him: he can't sit without support, so it isn't safe. Gait, heel–toe walking and Romberg once he can.
